pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change. -->

This PR allows self-hosters that have their own app store, to sync their user's 3rd party credentials with their instance of Cal.com. This allows their app store to be the source of truth for apps.

Fixes # (issue)

<!-- Please provide a loom video for visual changes to speed up reviews
 Loom Video: https://www.loom.com/
-->

## Requirement/Documentation

<!-- Please provide all documents that are important to understand the reason of that PR. -->

- If there is a requirement document, please, share it here.
- If there is ab UI/UX design document, please, share it here.

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [X] This change requires a documentation update

## How should this be tested?

<!-- Please describe the tests that you ran to verify your changes. Provide instructions so we can reproduce. Please also list any relevant details for your test configuration. Write details that help to start the tests -->

- Set up the required .env variables that were added in the PR
- Hit the `api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint with the correct webhook secret and encrypted payload
- The new credentials should be created in the DB
- For the affected apps, force a refresh of the tokens. The endpoint they are hitting should simulate what a self-hoster would have made
- Force a refresh of the tokens but this time do not enable app credential syncing

## Mandatory Tasks

- [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

<!-- Please remove all the irrelevant bullets to your PR -->

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- I haven't checked if new and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
pr.title: feat: Sync app credentials between Cal.com & self-hosted platforms

raw_findings.body: `prisma` is never imported in this file, so `prisma.credential.update` throws a ReferenceError at runtime, crashing every Salesforce calendar operation, not just the refresh path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Uncaught ReferenceError at runtime breaks Salesforce integration entirely.
raw_findings.impact: `prisma` is never imported in this file, so `prisma.credential.update` throws a ReferenceError at runtime, crashing every Salesforce calendar operation, not just the refresh path.
raw_findings.root_cause: New refresh/persist logic was added that calls `prisma.credential.update` without adding the corresponding import.
raw_findings.title: Salesforce getClient() uses undefined `prisma` without importing it
raw_findings.trigger: Any call to SalesforceCalendarService.getClient() (invoked from the constructor for every Salesforce credential) reaches the newly added refresh block.

raw_findings.body: The refreshed access_token/instance_url are persisted to the DB but the actual Connection returned to callers keeps using the old (possibly expired) access_token/instance_url, so the refresh has no effect on the current operation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Salesforce operations continue to use stale tokens immediately after a refresh was performed.
raw_findings.impact: The refreshed access_token/instance_url are persisted to the DB but the actual Connection returned to callers keeps using the old (possibly expired) access_token/instance_url, so the refresh has no effect on the current operation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new refresh code updates the DB but doesn't update the local `credentialKey` object used to build the returned client.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Merge `accessTokenParsed.data` into `credentialKey` (or use it directly) before constructing the returned `jsforce.Connection`.
raw_findings.title: Newly-fetched Salesforce access token/instance URL is never applied before creating the jsforce Connection
raw_findings.trigger: getClient() runs the newly added unconditional token refresh, then builds the jsforce.Connection using the pre-refresh `credentialKey` values.

raw_findings.body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a static string like "[object Object]", not a dynamic key, so the schema only really recognizes `access_token` and one bogus computed key; any real expiry/other properties returned by the self-hosted endpoint are silently stripped by zod's default 'strip unknown keys' behavior, losing expiry data after refresh.
raw_findings.evidence:
+const minimumTokenResponseSchema = z.object({
+  access_token: z.string(),
+  //   Assume that any property with a number is the expiry
+  [z.string().toString()]: z.number(),
+  //   Allow other properties in the token response
+  [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),
+});
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential-sync token refresh silently discards expiry/other fields, corrupting stored credentials.
raw_findings.impact: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a static string like "[object Object]", not a dynamic key, so the schema only really recognizes `access_token` and one bogus computed key; any real expiry/other properties returned by the self-hosted endpoint are silently stripped by zod's default 'strip unknown keys' behavior, losing expiry data after refresh.
raw_findings.root_cause: Misuse of dynamic object-key syntax with a Zod schema instance instead of an actual string literal/variable holding a field name.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the computed-key trick with an explicit schema, e.g. `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` or a schema that explicitly validates a named expiry field.
raw_findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed property keys don't validate arbitrary expiry fields
raw_findings.trigger: Any refresh performed while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set (the exact scenario this PR introduces).

raw_findings.body: The credential's refresh_token field gets overwritten with the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" instead of preserving the previous valid refresh token, corrupting the stored credential and breaking any future refresh flow that relies on it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stored refresh_token becomes a non-functional literal, breaking token refresh once sync is disabled or when fallback to normal OAuth refresh is needed.
raw_findings.impact: The credential's refresh_token field gets overwritten with the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" instead of preserving the previous valid refresh token, corrupting the stored credential and breaking any future refresh flow that relies on it.
raw_findings.root_cause: Placeholder/dummy value used instead of retaining the caller-provided refresh token when the sync endpoint doesn't return one.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the existing refresh_token (pass it through from the credential) instead of assigning a hardcoded placeholder string, or leave it undefined and merge with the prior credential value at the call site.
raw_findings.title: Missing refresh_token defaulted to the literal string "refresh_token"
raw_findings.trigger: A self-hosted CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT response (or any refresh response) that omits refresh_token, which is expected per the accompanying comment ('The response should only contain the access token and expiry date').

raw_findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safe-parse wrapper object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed key. This full wrapper object is now stored directly as `credential.key`, replacing the previous behavior of storing `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. Downstream code that reads `credential.key.access_token`/`refresh_token` etc. will get undefined, breaking Google Calendar auth after any refresh.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential row is corrupted with an incorrect shape, breaking subsequent Google Calendar API calls for that credential.
raw_findings.impact: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safe-parse wrapper object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed key. This full wrapper object is now stored directly as `credential.key`, replacing the previous behavior of storing `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. Downstream code that reads `credential.key.access_token`/`refresh_token` etc. will get undefined, breaking Google Calendar auth after any refresh.
raw_findings.root_cause: Replaced a direct `schema.parse()` call (which returns parsed data) with a function that returns a safeParse-style wrapper, without extracting `.data`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (and check `.success`) instead of assigning the whole return value to `key`.
raw_findings.title: Google Calendar refresh stores the full safeParse result object as the credential key
raw_findings.trigger: Any Google Calendar access-token refresh (`refreshAccessToken`) that reaches the credential-persist step.

raw_findings.body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response` object (no `.data` property), but the code immediately does `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, which throws a TypeError (`token` is undefined), breaking Google Calendar token refresh whenever credential sync is enabled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent/uncaught TypeError during refresh causes the calendar service to fall back to stale/invalid credentials.
raw_findings.impact: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response` object (no `.data` property), but the code immediately does `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, which throws a TypeError (`token` is undefined), breaking Google Calendar token refresh whenever credential sync is enabled.
raw_findings.root_cause: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response uniformly for the sync path, but call sites assume varying shapes based on their non-sync refreshFunction's return value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make refreshOAuthTokens's sync-mode return value shape-consistent with each integration's expectations (e.g. return `{ res: parsedJson }` for Google) or have each call site parse the JSON of the sync response explicitly.
raw_findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode, incompatible with Google's expected `.data` shape
raw_findings.trigger: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT both set with a userId present, causing refreshOAuthTokens to hit the sync branch.

raw_findings.body: In sync mode, the value assigned to `hubspotRefreshToken` is actually a raw fetch Response, not a `HubspotToken`. Subsequent code (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = ... hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000`) computes NaN and this malformed object is saved via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: hubspotRefreshToken as any } })`, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential.
raw_findings.evidence:
+        const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(
+          async () =>
+            await hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(
+              "refresh_token",
+              undefined,
+              WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/hubspot/callback",
+              this.client_id,
+              this.client_secret,
+              refreshToken
+            ),
+          "hubspot",
+          credential.userId
+        );
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential row silently corrupted with NaN/garbage fields when self-hosted sync is enabled.
raw_findings.impact: In sync mode, the value assigned to `hubspotRefreshToken` is actually a raw fetch Response, not a `HubspotToken`. Subsequent code (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = ... hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000`) computes NaN and this malformed object is saved via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: hubspotRefreshToken as any } })`, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential.
raw_findings.root_cause: Same as the Google case: refreshOAuthTokens's sync branch returns a raw Response while this call site expects a parsed HubspotToken object.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Parse the sync-mode response JSON into the expected `HubspotToken` shape before using it, or normalize refreshOAuthTokens' return type per integration.
raw_findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode, incompatible with Hubspot SDK token shape
raw_findings.trigger: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT both set with a userId present.

raw_findings.body: In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response with no `.data` property; the immediately-following `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined`), which is not caught in `refreshAccessToken`, crashing the refresh flow.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Uncaught TypeError crashes Zoho Bigin token refresh when self-hosted credential sync is enabled.
raw_findings.impact: In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response with no `.data` property; the immediately-following `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined`), which is not caught in `refreshAccessToken`, crashing the refresh flow.
raw_findings.root_cause: Same shared root cause: refreshOAuthTokens' sync branch always returns a raw Response object regardless of the shape callers require.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode return so `.data` is populated (e.g. parse the JSON response into `{ data: json }`) or branch handling per integration.
raw_findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode, incompatible with axios `.data` usage in Zoho Bigin
raw_findings.trigger: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT both set with a userId present, triggering a Zoho Bigin token refresh.

raw_findings.body: In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response with no `.data`; `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError, which is caught by the surrounding try/catch and effectively fails silently, leaving the Zoho CRM credential un-refreshed.
raw_findings.evidence:
+        const zohoCrmTokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(
+          async () =>
+            await axios({
+              method: "post",
+              url: url,
+              data: qs.stringify(formData),
+              headers: {
+                "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8",
+              },
+            }),
+          "zohocrm",
+          credential.userId
+        );
raw_findings.failure_mode: Token refresh silently fails when self-hosted credential sync is enabled, leaving stale Zoho CRM credentials.
raw_findings.impact: In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response with no `.data`; `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError, which is caught by the surrounding try/catch and effectively fails silently, leaving the Zoho CRM credential un-refreshed.
raw_findings.root_cause: Same shared root cause across integrations: refreshOAuthTokens' sync branch always returns a raw fetch Response.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode return value so `.data` matches what each integration's non-sync path returns.
raw_findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode, incompatible with axios `.data` usage in Zoho CRM
raw_findings.trigger: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT both set with a userId present, triggering a Zoho CRM token refresh.

raw_findings.body: The redirect URI no longer derives from `appConfig.slug`, so if the app's configured slug ever diverges from the literal string "zoho-bigin", the OAuth redirect will silently point to the wrong callback path, breaking installation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: OAuth redirect URI silently diverges from app config if the slug changes, causing broken installs.
raw_findings.impact: The redirect URI no longer derives from `appConfig.slug`, so if the app's configured slug ever diverges from the literal string "zoho-bigin", the OAuth redirect will silently point to the wrong callback path, breaking installation.
raw_findings.root_cause: Dynamic template interpolation was replaced with a hardcoded literal during this refactor, removing the single source of truth for the slug.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to keep the redirect URI in sync with app configuration.
raw_findings.title: Zoho Bigin redirect URI hardcodes slug instead of using appConfig.slug
raw_findings.trigger: This code path runs whenever the Zoho Bigin OAuth flow is initiated (GET request to this handler).

raw_findings.body: Using `!==` for secret comparison is vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks that could help an attacker incrementally guess the shared webhook secret.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Secret-guessing via response-time analysis is theoretically possible against the webhook endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: Using `!==` for secret comparison is vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks that could help an attacker incrementally guess the shared webhook secret.
raw_findings.root_cause: New authentication check for a sensitive webhook implemented with a simple string inequality check instead of a timing-safe comparison.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (after normalizing lengths/encoding) instead of `!==`.
raw_findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
raw_findings.trigger: Any request to the new /api/webhook/app-credential endpoint with an incorrect header value.

raw_findings.body: "CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET" is inserted after "CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY" instead of before it (and away from the other CALCOM_WEBHOOK_* entries), breaking the established alphabetical convention and making the list harder to scan/maintain.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reduced maintainability/readability of the globalEnv list convention.
raw_findings.impact: "CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET" is inserted after "CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY" instead of before it (and away from the other CALCOM_WEBHOOK_* entries), breaking the established alphabetical convention and making the list harder to scan/maintain.
raw_findings.root_cause: New env var was appended at an arbitrary position instead of in alphabetical order.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move "CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET" to be grouped alphabetically with the other CALCOM_ entries, immediately after "CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME" and before "CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY".
raw_findings.title: New CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET entry breaks alphabetical ordering of turbo.json globalEnv
raw_findings.trigger: Reading/maintaining the globalEnv list, which is otherwise alphabetically sorted.
